labels.description: The headline replaces "increasing interest rates" with "a higher interest rate environment" as a driver of benefit plan costs; the body is unchanged apart from a page-number artifact.
labels.rationale: Minor: the headline rewording names the same interest rate exposure with no change to the body, the other assumptions, or the severity language, and the only other difference is a page number.

labels.description: Adds a new sentence that recent spending by hyperscalers and others to support AI is beginning to pressure supply chains for semiconductors and other network components, and widens the offset discussion from cost pressures to "cost and supply pressures".
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a new supply-chain exposure (AI-driven demand for semiconductors and network components) is disclosed, stated as already beginning (criterion 3).

labels.description: Deletes the sentence stating that credit rating agencies have been applying tighter credit standards when evaluating debt levels and future growth prospects.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a previously disclosed adverse development (tighter rating agency standards affecting cost of borrowing) is removed, softening the risk (criterion 3).

labels.description: No change to the risk factor text; the only difference is a page number (8) that fell inside the prior-year body.
labels.rationale: Minor: the difference is a page-number layout artifact with no change in wording or substance.

labels.description: Drops the disclosure of AT&T's voluntary commitment to temporary C-Band precautionary measures near certain airports through January 1, 2028 in response to FAA radio altimeter concerns, and adds state rate regulation of broadband to the issues driving proposed legislation.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: a specific regulatory development (the FAA C-Band airport commitment) is dropped and a new regulatory issue (state rate regulation of broadband) is referenced.

labels.description: Replaces "climate change's impacts" with "its impacts" in the final sentence.
labels.rationale: Minor: stylistic rewording with identical meaning.

labels.description: Deletes the disclosure that the FCC's spectrum auction authority lapsed in 2023 and that the national spectrum strategy left spectrum availability uncertain, replaces the COVID-19 pandemic with "recent world events and trends", and adds the fixed wireless access product to the network expansion.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: a specific regulatory development (the lapse of FCC auction authority and the 2023 national spectrum strategy) and a named event (COVID-19) are dropped and a product (fixed wireless access) is added, removing a stated spectrum-availability uncertainty (criterion 1).

labels.description: No change to the risk factor text; the only difference is a page number (9) that now falls inside the current-year body.
labels.rationale: Minor: the difference is a page-number layout artifact with no change in wording or substance.

labels.description: Adds safety as a reputational factor and widens the litigation exposure from ordinary-course suits over employee misconduct to suits arising in or outside the ordinary course over misconduct by employees, contractors or other third parties.
labels.rationale: criterion 3: the scope of the litigation and reputation risk is widened to non-ordinary-course proceedings and to contractors and third parties, and safety is a newly disclosed factor (criterion 1).

labels.description: Adds customer use of mobile devices for AI-enabled applications as a driver of demand for higher-quality services.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a new demand driver (AI-enabled applications) behind the capital cost and supply chain risk is disclosed, widening its scope (criterion 3).
